note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer diagnosis with rising PSA and prior Gleason 4+4 biopsy results to determine optimal treatment strategy.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management. The patient is a 59-year-old ICT consultant, married, living with his partner. He has a history of hypertension and benign prostatic hyperplasia. Recent PSA trend shows a significant rise from 10.1 ng/mL in June 2023 to 25.0 ng/mL in January 2025, with a notable increase from 16.7 ng/mL in July 2024. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 3/35. He is an ex-smoker (13 pack-years, quit in 2005) and consumes 10 units of alcohol weekly. His lifestyle is sedentary with occasional walking. He lives over 90 minutes from the clinic and prefers phone follow-up where clinically safe. Recent appointments include a surveillance colonoscopy with gastroenterology and a pulmonary function test for known COPD follow-up.

Per rectum, the prostate feels asymmetrically enlarged with a firm, irregular nodule in the left lobe, consistent with clinical stage cT2c. General examination is unremarkable, with normal vital signs and no signs of distant metastasis.
